propositions.text: The Appellant, a South Korean citizen, appeals the RPD decision denying refugee protection.
propositions.quote: XXXX XXXX (the Appellant), a citizen of the Republic of Korea (South Korea), appeals a decision of the Refugee Protection Division (RPD) denying his claim for refugee protection.

propositions.text: The Appellant submitted no new evidence in support of his appeal.
propositions.quote: He has submitted no new evidence in support of his appeal.

propositions.text: The Appellant asks the RAD to set aside the RPD determination and substitute a positive determination.
propositions.quote: The Appellant asks the Refugee Appeal Division (RAD) to set aside the determination of the RPD and substitute a positive determination.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant appeals the RPD decision denying refugee protection, submits no new evidence, and asks the RAD to set aside the RPD decision and grant protection.

propositions.text: The RAD confirms the RPD decision that the Appellant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection and dismisses the appeal.
propositions.quote: Pursuant to Section 111(1)(a) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA), the RAD confirms the decision of the RPD that the Appellant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection. This appeal is dismissed.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD confirms the RPD decision denying refugee protection and dismisses the appeal.

propositions.text: The Appellant is a young man living in Canada since 2007 as an international student.
propositions.quote: The Appellant is a young man who has been living in Canada since 2007 as an international student.

propositions.text: He visited South Korea in 2014 and learned he would be required to perform military service upon return.
propositions.quote: He visited South Korea in XXXX of 2014 and learned that, upon return to his country, he would be required to perform military service.

propositions.text: He heard of problems in the South Korean military including hazing, beatings, and deaths.
propositions.quote: He heard of problems in the South Korean military, including hazing, beatings, and deaths.

propositions.text: He returned to Canada and made a refugee claim fearing harm during military service and imprisonment if he avoids it.
propositions.quote: He returned to Canada and thereafter made a refugee claim, fearing that he will be harmed during his military service and imprisoned if he avoids it.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant, a young man living in Canada since 2007, fears harm and imprisonment from South Korean military service and made a refugee claim.

propositions.text: The RPD heard the Appellant's refugee claim on August 27, 2015 and rejected it on August 31, 2015.
propositions.quote: The Appellant's application for refugee protection was heard on August 27, 2015. By a decision of August 31, 2015, the RPD rejected the claim.

propositions.text: The RPD found no nexus between the Appellant's fears and a Convention ground.
propositions.quote: The panel concluded that there is no nexus between the Appellant's fears and a Convention ground.

propositions.text: South Korea's conscription law is general, not inherently persecutory, and sanctions do not amount to cruel or unusual treatment or torture.
propositions.quote: It found that South Korea's conscription law is one of general application, is not inherently persecutory, and that the sanctions for violating that law do not amount to cruel and unusual treatment or punishment or torture.

propositions.text: The RPD dismissed the claim that the Appellant will be bullied for being 'Westernized'.
propositions.quote: The RPD also dismissed as unproven the Appellant's claim that he will be bullied in the military because he is "Westernized" as a result of his time spent in Canada.

propositions.text: The RPD rejected the argument that refusal to join military is political expression or conscientious objection.
propositions.quote: The panel did not accept the Appellant's argument that his refusal to join the military is a form of political expression, nor did it find that the Appellant is a conscientious objector to military service.

propositions.text: Punishment for evading service (18 months to 3 years imprisonment) is not excessive or persecutory.
propositions.quote: It found that the punishment for evading service-between 18 months and three years' imprisonment-is not excessive or persecutory.

propositions.text: The RPD concluded the South Korean government is actively addressing military problems and protection is available.
propositions.quote: The RPD also concluded that, as the South Korean government is actively addressing problems in the military, and that the Appellant can avail himself of protection.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD rejected the refugee claim, finding no nexus to a Convention ground, conscription law is general, sanctions not cruel, bullying claim unproven, no political expression or conscientious objection, punishment not persecutory, and state protection available.

propositions.text: The Appellant argues the RPD erred by failing to recognize military torture as persecutory and opposition to hazing relates to a Convention ground.
propositions.quote: The Appellant argues on appeal that the RPD made many errors in rejecting his claim, including failing to understand that torture in the military can in itself be persecutory, in failing to appreciate torture and hazing is not punishment pursuant to a law of general application, in failing to recognize that opposition to hazing and torture is related to a Convention ground, and in making a finding of state protection based on the serious efforts of the authorities, without considering whether those efforts have had practical results.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant argues the RPD erred by not recognizing military torture as persecutory, opposition to hazing relates to a Convention ground, and state protection findings lacked practical assessment.

propositions.text: IRPA sets grounds and remedies for appeal but does not specify the RAD's standard of review.
propositions.quote: While the IRPA sets out grounds for appeal as well as possible remedies, it does not specify the standard by which the RAD is to review the decision of the lower tribunal.

paragraphs.summary: IRPA provides appeal grounds and remedies but does not specify the RAD's standard of review.

propositions.text: The Appellant makes no specific submissions on the standard of intervention to be applied by the RAD.
propositions.quote: The Appellant makes no specific submissions with respect to the standard of intervention to be applied here.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant makes no specific submissions on the RAD's standard of intervention.

propositions.text: The panel previously considered legislation and jurisprudence on the RAD's role and deference to RPD findings.
propositions.quote: In another decision, this panel considered at some length the legislation and jurisprudence concerning the role of the RAD.1 It assessed the nature of a RAD appeal and addressed the scope and degree of deference to be shown to findings of the RPD.

propositions.text: The panel's prior conclusions on RAD appeals apply here.
propositions.quote: The panel reached the following conclusions, which it finds to also be applicable here, about the approach to be taken in a RAD appeal.

paragraphs.summary: The panel previously considered the RAD's role and deference to RPD findings and finds those conclusions applicable here.

propositions.text: The RAD will assess all evidence, including admissible new evidence, and consider law, fact, and mixed questions raised by parties.
propositions.quote: The RAD will take the following approach in considering an appeal against a decision of the RPD. It will assess all of the evidence, both that in the RPD's record and any admissible new evidence. It will consider questions of law, fact, and mixed law and fact raised by the Appellant and, where applicable, the Respondent.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD will assess all evidence and consider legal and factual questions raised by the parties.

propositions.text: In a true appeal with no new evidence, the RAD independently assesses the RPD record to determine if the RPD was wrong.
propositions.quote: Where the proceeding is a true appeal-that is, where there is no admissible new evidence-the RAD will consider the decision of the RPD, the submissions in respect of that decision, and determine whether the RPD's determination is wrong. As a true appeal is founded on the record, the RAD must conduct an independent assessment of the evidence in that record in order to determine the appeal.

paragraphs.summary: In a true appeal without new evidence, the RAD independently assesses the RPD record to decide if the RPD was wrong.

propositions.text: In a hybrid appeal with admissible new evidence showing RPD error, the RAD considers the RPD's reasons in light of new evidence.
propositions.quote: Where an appeal includes admissible new evidence that speaks to an error in the RPD's decision, it is a hybrid appeal, where the RAD must consider the RPD's reasons in light of the new evidence, which may establish that the decision of the RPD is wrong.

paragraphs.summary: In a hybrid appeal with new evidence showing RPD error, the RAD considers the RPD's reasons with the new evidence.

propositions.text: In a limited de novo appeal with new evidence changing the claim, the RAD considers both new evidence and RPD record and findings.
propositions.quote: Where an appeal presents admissible new evidence which establishes a new, changed, or heightened risk, or otherwise changes the overall nature of the claim, this will result in a limited de novo appeal. In some such cases, the decision of the RPD may be less relevant in light of the new evidence-that is, the new evidence establishes a risk or degree of risk, or other potentially determinative matter not considered by the RPD. Unlike a true de novo proceeding, however, the RAD will not ignore the RPD's record or the findings of the lower tribunal, as these may remain relevant to the appeal.

paragraphs.summary: In a limited de novo appeal with new evidence changing the claim, the RAD considers both new evidence and the RPD record and findings.

propositions.text: The RAD defers to RPD findings made from an advantageous position, such as credibility and fact findings, unless reasoning is incomprehensible or unsupported.
propositions.quote: The RAD will recognize and respect findings which the RPD was in an advantageous position to make, which will normally include credibility findings and other findings of fact. Where such deference is to be shown, the RAD will not intervene unless the RPD's reasoning process is not comprehensible or the outcome of that process is not based on and supported by the evidence.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD defers to RPD findings made from an advantageous position unless reasoning is incomprehensible or unsupported.

propositions.text: Where RPD determination is based on findings warranting deference, the RAD assesses if reasoning is comprehensible and evidence-based.
propositions.quote: Where the RPD's determination is entirely based on findings which warrant deference-such as an overall lack of credibility, based on oral testimony-the RAD will, having conducted its own assessment of the evidence, consider whether the RPD's reasoning process is comprehensible and whether the determination is based on and supported by the evidence.

paragraphs.summary: Where RPD's determination is based on findings warranting deference, the RAD checks if reasoning is comprehensible and supported by evidence.

propositions.text: On matters where RPD has no advantage, RAD applies correctness standard and substitutes its own findings if it disagrees.
propositions.quote: On matters where the RPD has no advantage, the RAD will show no deference and will apply a standard of correctness, engaging in its own analysis of the evidence and reaching its own conclusion to determine if the RPD was wrong. Where the RAD finds that its conclusion does not agree with that of the RPD, the RAD will substitute its own finding and determination or, if it is unable to substitute, will refer the matter back to the RPD for redetermination.

paragraphs.summary: Where RPD has no advantage, RAD applies correctness standard and substitutes its own findings if it disagrees.

propositions.text: The RAD agrees the RPD made errors including mischaracterizing conscientious objection and failing to assess practical outcomes of state protection efforts.
propositions.quote: The RAD agrees with the Appellant that the RPD made several errors in determining his refugee claim. Although he did not claim to be a conscientious objector, the RPD repeatedly referred to conscientious objection as an issue, before finding that the Appellant's "personal goals do not qualify him as a true conscientious objector". The RPD also considered efforts made by the South Korean government to combat hazing and abuse in the military, and it concluded that "there is protection and recourse offered", without considering whether the state's efforts had any practical outcome or resulted in adequate protection.

propositions.text: The RPD erred in comparing South Korean conscription military to volunteer forces of Canada and the U.S.
propositions.quote: It was also wrong, as the Appellant points out on appeal, for the RPD to compare the South Korea military to others: "Sadly, there have been documented cases [of bullying] in Canada and the U.S.A. armed forces." The conscription-based South Korean military is not comparable to the volunteer armed forces of Canada and the U.S., even more so given that South Korea's conscripts are continually faced with the prospect of fighting against one of the largest militaries in the world.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds RPD erred by mischaracterizing conscientious objection, failing to assess practical state protection, and wrongly comparing South Korean conscription military to volunteer forces.

propositions.text: The RPD had no advantage over the RAD in assessing objective evidence about risk, state protection, or nexus to a Convention ground.
propositions.quote: However, these errors are not dispositive of this appeal. The RPD had no particular advantage over the RAD in assessing objective evidence about the risk faced by the Appellant, or in considering the adequacy of state protection, or whether there is nexus between his claim and a Convention ground.

propositions.text: The RAD will conduct a full independent assessment of the evidence and make its own determination on the refugee claim.
propositions.quote: The RAD must conduct a full, independent assessment of the evidence in the record, and, on that basis, it is able to come to its own determination of the Appellant's refugee claim.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD had no advantage on objective evidence; the RAD will independently assess evidence and determine the refugee claim.

propositions.text: The RPD made no credibility findings against the Appellant; he is presumed truthful and that presumption is unrebutted.
propositions.quote: It is important to note here that the RPD did not make any credibility findings with respect to the Appellant. He is entitled to the presumption of truthfulness, and that presumption has not been rebutted.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD made no adverse credibility findings; the Appellant is presumed truthful and that presumption is unrebutted.

propositions.text: The key issues are nexus, risk of harm, state protection, and whether evading military service results in cruel or unusual punishment or torture.
propositions.quote: The RAD finds that the key issues to be determined here are nexus, risk of harm, state protection, and whether the Appellant faces cruel and unusual punishment, or torture, if he chooses to evade military service.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD identifies nexus, risk, state protection, and punishment severity as key issues.

propositions.text: The Appellant is not opposed to military service and believes in defending his country.
propositions.quote: The Appellant is not opposed to military service itself, and he believes in the need to defend his country.

propositions.text: He fears hazing, bullying, or torture during military service, making him reluctant to join.
propositions.quote: He fears that he will be hazed, bullied, or tortured during his military service, and that fear of abuse makes him reluctant to join the military.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant supports military service but fears hazing and torture, making him reluctant to join.

propositions.text: Refusal to perform compulsory military service is a political opinion rejecting state military recruitment.
propositions.quote: his refusal to perform compulsory military service "is a clear political opinion rejecting the state mechanism of recruiting into the military institution"

propositions.text: Fear of torture and hazing amounts to an imputed opinion rejecting state recruitment, creating nexus to a Convention ground.
propositions.quote: his fear of torture and hazing amounts to an imputed opinion rejecting the state mechanism, creating a nexus to a Convention ground

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant argues refusal of military service is political opinion and fear of torture creates nexus to a Convention ground.

propositions.text: Appellant fears abuse after conscription, not opposition to conscription itself.
propositions.quote: the Appellant is not opposed to the state mechanism of recruitment-conscription-but rather fears illegitimate abuse that he might suffer once conscripted

propositions.text: Abuse feared is not state-prescribed; government shows interest in protecting conscripts' human rights.
propositions.quote: The abuse he fears is not prescribed or required by the state; in fact, the government and the military have shown interest in protecting the human rights of conscripts

propositions.text: Appellant fears targeting as conscript, not for anti-hazing views.
propositions.quote: he fears that he will be targeted because he is a conscript

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Appellant fears abuse after conscription, not conscription itself, and fears targeting as conscript, not for anti-hazing views.

propositions.text: Appellant fears being singled out as "Westernized" after living in Canada.
propositions.quote: The Appellant does fear that he will be singled out because he is "Westernized" after some years of living in Canada

propositions.text: Appellant provided no evidence that "Westernized" individuals are targeted; contention appears speculative.
propositions.quote: He has not provided evidence, however, to establish that individuals seen as "Westernized" are targeted, and his contention therefore appears to be speculative

paragraphs.summary: Appellant fears targeting as "Westernized" but provides no evidence; court finds this speculative.

propositions.text: Appellant argues he will be jailed for political opinion opposing hazing and torture.
propositions.quote: he will be jailed because of his political opinion-that is, he is opposed to hazing and torture, will therefore refuse military service, and as a consequence will be imprisoned

propositions.text: Jailing would be for evading military service, not for political opinion.
propositions.quote: If he is jailed, it will be for evading military service

propositions.text: Evasion is due to fear of personal harm, not political opinion but self-preservation.
propositions.quote: If he evades military service, it is because he fears personal harm and injury. This may well be self-preservation, but it is not political opinion

paragraphs.summary: Appellant argues jail for political opinion; court finds jail would be for evasion due to fear, not political opinion.

propositions.text: No nexus between Appellant's refugee claim and a Convention ground found.
propositions.quote: there is no nexus between the Appellant's refugee claim and a Convention ground

propositions.text: Claim falls under Section 97, not Section 96, of IRPA.
propositions.quote: the claim does not fall under Section 96, but must be considered under Section 97 of the IRPA

paragraphs.summary: Court finds no nexus to Convention ground; claim considered under IRPA Section 97, not Section 96.

propositions.text: Whether removal to South Korea poses personal danger of torture or cruel treatment to Appellant.
propositions.quote: Would the Appellant's removal to South Korea subject him personally to a danger of torture, or a risk to life or of cruel and unusual treatment or punishment?

propositions.text: Risk assessed by whether it is more likely than not individual would face such risk if returned.
propositions.quote: the question is whether "it is more likely than not that the individual would be subjected, personally, to a risk to his life or to a risk of cruel and unusual treatment or punishment if the person was returned to his country of nationality."

paragraphs.summary: Court frames issue of risk of torture or cruel treatment on return, citing legal standard of 'more likely than not'.

propositions.text: There is serious risk to all conscripts; physical abuse tolerated; suicide rates very high in South Korean military.
propositions.quote: there is a serious risk to all conscripts, that physical abuse is tolerated, and that suicide rates are very high in the South Korean military

paragraphs.summary: Appellant argues serious risk of abuse and high suicide rates for conscripts in South Korean military.

propositions.text: Abuse of conscripts is serious in South Korea with many hazing and brutality examples.
propositions.quote: abuse of conscripts is a serious issue in South Korea; there are many examples of hazing and brutality

propositions.text: 3300 reported assault cases in five years in military of over 600,000 members; about 0.1% affected annually.
propositions.quote: in the past five years, there have been about 3300 reported cases of assault and brutality in the South Korean armed forces

propositions.text: Even accounting for unreported cases, abuse affects just over 1% of soldiers annually.
propositions.quote: even if there are ten unreported cases for each reported instance, this would increase the percentage to just over one percent

paragraphs.summary: Court finds abuse serious but affects a small percentage of soldiers, even considering unreported cases.

propositions.text: Physical violence is uncommon; hazing changed to non-violent punishments after investigation.
propositions.quote: physical violence is uncommon; as a result of a "major investigation into violence in the barracks", hazing changed to punishing people with "absurdities"

paragraphs.summary: Court finds physical violence uncommon; hazing replaced by non-violent punishments after investigation.

propositions.text: Suicide rates in South Korean military are much higher than in U.S. armed forces.
propositions.quote: suicide rates in the South Korean military are much higher than in the U.S. armed forces

propositions.text: Suicide rates in South Korea are highest worldwide, even outside military.
propositions.quote: Suicide rates in South Korea-even outside the military-are the highest in the world

propositions.text: Military suicide rates reflect poor mental health and stress, not risk of hazing or abuse.
propositions.quote: The suicide rate in the military may be indicative of poor mental health screening and services, of a stressful environment, and of many other factors; it does not assist in assessing the risk of hazing or other abuse

paragraphs.summary: Appellant cites high military suicide rates; court finds this reflects broader issues, not hazing risk.

propositions.text: Hazing and abuse are significant but risk to Appellant is not more likely than not for torture or cruel treatment.
propositions.quote: it is not more likely than not that the Appellant would be subject to a danger of torture, or to a risk to life or of cruel and unusual treatment or punishment

paragraphs.summary: Court finds risk of torture or cruel treatment to Appellant not more likely than not despite hazing problems.

propositions.text: Even if risk found, refugee claim would be rejected on basis of state protection.
propositions.quote: Even if the RAD had reached the opposite conclusion, it would nevertheless reject this refugee claim on the basis of state protection

paragraphs.summary: Court states it would reject claim on state protection grounds even if risk found.

propositions.text: RPD noted government efforts to reduce military abuse but did not assess concrete results or adequacy of protection.
propositions.quote: The RPD pointed to serious efforts made by the South Korean government to reduce abuse in the military. That analysis was incomplete; the RPD was required to consider whether those serious efforts had concrete results, leading to adequate state protection

paragraphs.summary: Court finds RPD's analysis incomplete for not assessing concrete results of government efforts and adequacy of protection.

propositions.text: High-profile cases of military bullying and abuse led to government pledges and reforms.
propositions.quote: There have been a number of high-profile cases in South Korea in which conscripts have committed suicide or killed their fellow soldiers as a result of suffering bullying and abuse

propositions.text: Government increased human rights instructors and launched Military Human Rights Team.
propositions.quote: the defence ministry set up a human rights council and increased the number of human rights instructors from 250 to 2000, while the National Human Rights Council launched a Military Human Rights Team

propositions.text: Government eased exemption standards for mental illness to identify at-risk individuals.
propositions.quote: The government introduced a number of measures to better identify individuals who are at higher risk of "succumbing" to the harsh military environment, including an easing of the standards by which exemptions are granted for mental illness

paragraphs.summary: Court details government reforms and increased human rights efforts following high-profile military abuse cases.

propositions.text: Army under close government scrutiny; measures led to criminal cases and resignations.
propositions.quote: The army is under close scrutiny by the government, and the state's efforts have had concrete results. Three hundred criminal cases were filed in the military for hazing and mistreatment of soldiers

propositions.text: High-profile tragedy led to army chief resignation and suspension of operations for human rights session.
propositions.quote: After one high-profile tragedy, the army's chief of staff resigned, and the entire army suspended operations for a day-long session on human rights

propositions.text: Charges upgraded, officers charged and dismissed, and improvements made to leave and barracks.
propositions.quote: Charges against soldiers alleged to have killed a conscript were upgraded from manslaughter to murder. Officers have been charged for not reporting abuse and dismissed from their posts. The Ministry of National Defense has improved leave, allowed more family visits, and renovated barracks to be "friendlier places"

propositions.text: New communication line uncovered 4000 previously unreported abuses.
propositions.quote: A new public line of communications on the issue of bullying has uncovered 4000 instances of previously unreported abuses

paragraphs.summary: Court finds government scrutiny led to criminal cases, resignations, improved conditions, and uncovering unreported abuses.

propositions.text: Justice system sometimes lenient with military abuse cases.
propositions.quote: the South Korean justice system does not always deal appropriately with abuses in the military; there are examples of lenient sentences given to senior soldiers

propositions.text: Over 1000 punishments administered for 3300 assault cases, including prison and probation sentences.
propositions.quote: more than a thousand have resulted in punishment being administered, including fifty prison sentences, more than 350 probation sentences, about 150 suspended sentences, and more than 400 fines

propositions.text: Authorities take action and punish offenders; some murder convictions led to long prison terms.
propositions.quote: it is clear that the authorities do take action and administer punishment. Other evidence indicates that soldiers convicted of murdering a conscript were sentenced to as much as 45 years in prison

paragraphs.summary: Court finds justice system punishes many military abuse cases, though sometimes lenient, with serious sentences for murder.

propositions.text: Presumption that South Korea provides adequate protection to citizens, including military.
propositions.quote: There is a presumption that South Korea, a functioning democracy, can provide adequate protection to its citizens, including those in the military

propositions.text: Appellant must rebut presumption with clear and convincing evidence.
propositions.quote: It is for the Appellant here to rebut that presumption with clear and convincing evidence

propositions.text: Appellant has no personal evidence to rebut presumption, relies on mixed objective evidence.
propositions.quote: He has no personal evidence with which to rebut the presumption, and he therefore relies upon objective evidence. The RAD has carefully reviewed that evidence and finds it to be mixed

propositions.text: Authorities aware of abuse problem, taken significant steps with concrete outcomes including criminal charges and imprisonment.
propositions.quote: There is evidence that the South Korean authorities are aware of the problem of abuse in the military, have taken significant steps to address the issue, and that such measures have had concrete outcomes, including criminal charges and imprisonment

propositions.text: Protection is imperfect but Appellant has not rebutted presumption of adequate state protection.
propositions.quote: It is clear that the protection provided by the state here is not perfect. However, the RAD finds that the Appellant has not provided clear and convincing evidence to rebut the presumption of adequate state protection

paragraphs.summary: Court states presumption of adequate protection; Appellant lacks clear evidence to rebut it despite imperfections.

propositions.text: Even if risk of harm found, claim rejected and appeal dismissed on state protection basis.
propositions.quote: Even if the RAD had concluded that the Appellant faces a risk of harm upon return to South Korea, it would reject his refugee claim, and dismiss his appeal, on the basis of state protection

paragraphs.summary: Court would reject claim and dismiss appeal on state protection grounds even if risk found.

propositions.text: Appellant argues he will be imprisoned for refusing military service and face abuse in prison.
propositions.quote: The Appellant argues on appeal that he will be imprisoned for refusing to complete his military service, and that he faces abuse in prison

paragraphs.summary: Appellant argues imprisonment for refusal and abuse in prison.

propositions.text: South Korea imprisons hundreds of conscientious objectors yearly; refusal punishable by up to 18 months.
propositions.quote: South Korea imprisons hundreds of conscientious objectors each year. Refusal to carry out military service is punishable by up to eighteen months in prison

propositions.text: No evidence shows those refusing military service face abuse or mistreatment in prison.
propositions.quote: the Appellant has not pointed to any evidence to show that those who refuse military service face abuse or mistreatment in prison

paragraphs.summary: Court finds refusal leads to imprisonment but no evidence of abuse in prison for objectors.

propositions.text: Prison conditions in South Korea meet international standards and allow visits by independent observers.
propositions.quote: Prison conditions in South Korea meet international standards, and the government permits visits by independent observers.

propositions.text: Prisoners can report mistreatment to a Reporting Centre that investigates and refers cases for correction.
propositions.quote: Prisoners can report mistreatment to the Reporting Centre for Human Rights Infringement, which investigates and can and does refer cases for correction.

propositions.text: Food, sanitation, and medical care in South Korean prisons are adequate.
propositions.quote: Food, sanitation, and medical care are adequate.

propositions.text: Authorities investigate credible complaints and document investigations publicly.
propositions.quote: Authorities investigate credible complaints of problematic conditions and document their investigations in a publicly-accessible manner.

propositions.text: Prisoners have reasonable access to visitors.
propositions.quote: Prisoners have reasonable access to visitors.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds South Korean prison conditions meet international standards, allow independent visits, have adequate care, investigate complaints, and allow visitor access.

propositions.text: An eighteen-month prison sentence is not cruel or unusual and is less than mandatory two-year military service.
propositions.quote: there is nothing cruel and unusual about a prison sentence of eighteen months, which is actually less than the mandatory two-year military service.

propositions.text: The Appellant has not shown the punishment is disproportionate or against international standards.
propositions.quote: The Appellant has not shown that this punishment is disproportionate or out of line with international standards.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the eighteen-month sentence is not cruel or unusual and the Appellant failed to show it is disproportionate or against international standards.

propositions.text: Refusing military service will make employment more difficult for the Appellant.
propositions.quote: The Appellant claims that, if he refuses to complete his military service, it will be more difficult for him to obtain employment.

propositions.text: Objective evidence supports the claim that refusal causes employment difficulty.
propositions.quote: This assertion is supported by objective evidence.

propositions.text: Employment difficulty is discriminatory but does not amount to persecution.
propositions.quote: such difficulty, while discriminatory, does not amount to persecution.

propositions.text: No evidence shows imprisoned objectors were unable to find employment.
propositions.quote: there is no evidence that some, most, or all of these individuals were unable to find employment.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant claims refusal causes employment difficulty; the court finds this discriminatory but not persecution and no evidence of employment denial for imprisoned objectors.

propositions.text: The RAD finds the Appellant's refugee claim must fail for all these reasons.
propositions.quote: For all of these reasons, the RAD finds that the Appellant's refugee claim must fail.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD concludes the Appellant's refugee claim must fail for all stated reasons.

propositions.text: The Appellant cites other reasons to remain in Canada, including his mother's human trafficking victim status and dependence on him.
propositions.quote: The Appellant, in his Basis of Claim, sets out other reasons for which he wishes to remain in Canada. His mother is a victim of human trafficking and depends heavily on the Appellant and his brother.

propositions.text: The RAD is sympathetic but cannot consider this humanitarian situation, best addressed elsewhere.
propositions.quote: The RAD is sympathetic to this difficult situation; unfortunately, it is not a matter which this tribunal can consider, but one which is best addressed in a humanitarian and compassionate context.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant cites family hardship; the RAD is sympathetic but says it cannot consider this humanitarian matter.

propositions.text: Pursuant to IRPA, the RAD confirms the RPD decision that the Appellant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection.
propositions.quote: Pursuant to Section 111(1)(a) of the IRPA, the RAD confirms the decision of the RPD that the Appellant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection.

propositions.text: The appeal is dismissed.
propositions.quote: This appeal is dismissed.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD confirms the RPD decision denying refugee status and dismisses the appeal.
